vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.1.2

The skill bundle facilitates automated data collection from social media platforms (Douyin, TikTok, Xiaohongshu) using a local bridge and browser extension. It contains high-risk execution patterns, specifically the use of `bash -lc` to execute arbitrary commands provided via the `--bridge-cmd` argument in `collect_and_export_loop.sh`, and a remote execution feature in `run.sh` that uses SSH to run scripts on a remote host. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated purpose of managing a collection bridge, the lack of input sanitization and the presence of hardcoded developer paths (e.g., `/Users/zhym/coding/...`) and specific external dependencies (Meixi connector) warrant a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (local browser-extension data collection via a local bridge); it requires curl/node and runs bundled shell scripts that talk to a localhost bridge — no unrelated credentials or remote download/install steps are required — but the scripts do execute user-supplied commands (bridge startup) and optionally support SSH, so review before running in sensitive environments.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match what is implemented: the scripts call a local HTTP bridge at 127.0.0.1:19820 and use curl/node to POST /api/collect and poll /api/tasks. Required binaries (curl, node) are appropriate for the claimed functionality and there are no unrelated credentials or surprising external service dependencies.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts stick to the collection/export workflow against a local bridge and a browser extension. However the scripts allow starting an arbitrary bridge command (BRIDGE_CMD) via nohup bash -lc and support remote execution via SSH when WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH is set. Those behaviors are coherent with starting/controlling the connector but give the skill the ability to run arbitrary commands if caller supplies them — review any BRIDGE_CMD or environment variables before use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or remote downloads; this is an instruction-only skill with bundled shell scripts. Nothing is fetched from arbitrary URLs or written to system locations by automatic installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables or secrets are declared. The scripts optionally read environment variables (e.g., WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD/BRIDGE_URL) to enable remote SSH or a custom bridge startup command; these optional vars can change behavior significantly, so they should only be set when you trust the target host/command.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no special persistent installation is requested. The skill can be invoked autonomously (platform default), and its scripts execute local shell commands as expected for a CLI wrapper. There is no evidence it modifies other skills or system-wide agent configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose, but it runs shell scripts that will: (1) talk to a local bridge on 127.0.0.1:19820, (2) optionally start a bridge process using a user-supplied BRIDGE_CMD (which will be executed via nohup bash -lc), and (3) optionally SSH to a remote host if WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH is set. Before installing or running: review the included scripts (collect_and_export_loop.sh and run.sh), do not set WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH or WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD unless you control/trust the remote host and command, avoid passing untrusted BRIDGE_CMD, and run the skill in an isolated environment if you are concerned about arbitrary command execution. If you only want to inspect behavior, run with verbose logging and without --ensure-bridge so the skill will fail rather than attempt to start a bridge automatically.
